**Delete originals after encoding (optional).** The Add sheet has a new checkbox, "Delete original when done". When it's on, each source file is moved to the Recycle Bin (Trash on macOS) after its new file is finished and checked: every frame encoded, the mux succeeded, and the new file lasts as long as the source. Test clips never delete, and anything that doesn't check out keeps the original with a warning in the episode log. It's off by default. Network drives have no Recycle Bin, so there the original is deleted for good.

The same option is `"DeleteSource": true` in `upscale-settings.json`, or `--set DeleteSource=true` for `upscale-cli`.

## Also in this release

- The episode log's reason for the default audio language now labels 4- and 5-channel tracks as 4.0 and 5.0 (it said 3.1 and 4.1). Track names were already right.

## Files

- `Upscale_0.1.2_x64-setup.exe`: Windows installer (unsigned: SmartScreen may warn, More info → Run anyway).
- `Upscale_0.1.2_aarch64.dmg`: macOS app, experimental (ad-hoc signed: right-click → Open the first time).
- `upscale-cli.exe`, `upscale-cli-macos-arm64.tar.gz`: the command-line versions.
- `latest.json`, `Upscale_0.1.2_aarch64.app.tar.gz`: used by the in-app updater.
